find: Officers may stop and search a person if they have reasonable grounds to suspect the individual is carrying weapons, stolen goods or articles for use in crime.
replace: Officers usually need reasonable grounds to suspect a person has weapons, stolen goods or articles for use in crime. In limited circumstances, a senior officer can authorise searches without individual suspicion.
note: F8: Authorised no-suspicion stop-and-search powers are an exception.

replace: Police usually need reasonable grounds to suspect someone is carrying weapons, stolen goods or items for use in crime. In limited circumstances, a senior officer can authorise searches without individual suspicion.
note: F8: The word ‘only’ wrongly excludes authorised no-suspicion powers.

find: Magistrates can impose fines, community sentences and custodial sentences of up to six months for a single offence (or twelve months for multiple offences).
replace: Magistrates can impose fines and community sentences. They can impose up to six months’ custody for a summary offence and up to twelve months for an either-way offence.
note: F10: The custodial maximum depends on whether the offence is summary or either-way.

value: Up to 12 months for an either-way offence; up to 6 months for a summary offence.
note: F10: The previous answer gave an incorrect universal maximum.

find: At age 16, a person in England, Wales and Northern Ireland may consent to medical treatment, marry with parental consent, leave school, work full-time and join the armed forces with parental consent.

find: The Northern Ireland Assembly can legislate on devolved matters, while Westminster retains control over reserved areas including criminal justice policy in many instances.
replace: The Northern Ireland Assembly can legislate on devolved matters, including policing and justice. Westminster retains control of reserved and excepted matters, such as immigration and national security.
note: F12: Policing and justice are transferred matters in Northern Ireland.

find: Prisons have high reoffending rates — around half of adults released from custody go on to commit further offences within one year.
replace: Official data for the April–June 2024 cohort showed that 67.1% of adults released after sentences under 12 months committed a proven reoffence within a year.
note: F13: Replace an unsupported generalisation with the current official figure for short custodial sentences.

find: Key principles of the Geneva Conventions include: the prohibition on targeting civilians, the requirement to treat prisoners of war humanely, the protection of medical personnel and facilities, and the ban on using certain weapons such as chemical weapons and landmines.
replace: Key rules of international humanitarian law include protecting civilians, treating prisoners of war humanely and protecting medical personnel and facilities. Separate treaties ban chemical weapons and anti-personnel landmines.
note: F14: The weapons bans are not provisions of the Geneva Conventions themselves.

find: To become a magistrate, a person must apply to the Judicial Appointments Commission and be assessed for qualities including good character, social awareness, sound judgement and the ability to see things from another’s perspective.
replace: To become a magistrate, a person applies through a local Advisory Committee on Justices of the Peace and is assessed for qualities including good character, social awareness, sound judgement and the ability to see things from another’s perspective.
note: F15: The Judicial Appointments Commission does not recruit magistrates.

find: Asylum seekers are not the same as illegal immigrants; applying for asylum is a legal right under international law, established by the 1951 UN Refugee Convention.
replace: Asylum seekers are not the same as illegal immigrants; the right to seek asylum is recognised in Article 14 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and the 1951 UN Refugee Convention defines who counts as a refugee and the protection they must be given.
note: The 1951 Convention defines refugee status; the right to seek asylum comes from UDHR Article 14 (Codex ADJ ruled FIX).
